title: Legal-hold-aware soft-delete with replayable purge simulation and certified completion receipts
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers need an auditable, low-risk way to validate automated right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) workflows before irreversible deletion runs in production. Current purge tooling in Redwood supports scheduled and on-demand deletion but lacks an integrated sandboxed verification path that respects legal holds and produces tamper-evident receipts for compliance teams.

Objective: Ship a feature set that lets customers (1) run replayable, read-only purge simulations against a safe snapshot; (2) ensure legal-hold and retention overrides are always honored by the purge engine; (3) produce cryptographically verifiable completion receipts and an evidence bundle (logs, record lists, checksums) that can be exported to the customer or uploaded to their audit store. The flow should work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and integrate with existing retention and residency rules in the control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can trigger a 'purge simulation' that runs a deterministic, read-only replay of the purge plan against a time-bound snapshot without modifying primary data stores.
Simulation honors all active legal holds, retention flags, and residency restrictions; any suppressed records are listed in the simulation report with reasons.
Production purge runs remain default for irreversible deletes; an explicit opt-in flag enables sandboxed simulation mode in the Console and API.

After a successful real purge, the system emits a signed completion receipt containing: purge id, record checksums, record counts by residency zone, start/end timestamps, and a cryptographic signature verifiable with Redwood's public key.
Evidence bundle (logs, delta manifests, checksum file, simulation vs actual diff) can be downloaded from the Console or streamed to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket via subscription webhook.
All UI and API actions related to simulation and purge must be audit-logged with token and actor metadata visible in the Console timeline.
Feature is covered by automated integration tests that run simulation and real purge flows in a CI environment and assert receipts/checksums match expected deterministic values.
Security review completed and approved by Security and Legal before GA release.
implementation_notes: Create a snapshot API that can produce a consistent read view (MVCC or object-store manifest) for the simulation runner.
Extend the existing purge planner to emit a deterministic plan file that both simulation and execution engines consume; plan includes reasons for suppression (legal hold, retention, residency).
Build a simulation runner that executes the planner in read-only mode, generating the evidence bundle and a simulation report with per-record status.
Add cryptographic signing service (using KMS) to produce receipts; public key will be published for customer verification.
Add Console UI: 'Run Simulation' button, progress view, and 'Download Evidence Bundle' action; API endpoint: POST /v1/purges/simulate.
For Private deployments, provide a local signer adapter that integrates with customer HSM/KMS; fallback to Redwood signer only with explicit customer opt-in.
Performance: simulation runs should be rate-limited and scheduled to avoid impacting production inference latency; recommend running large-scope simulations during configured maintenance windows.
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Martinez: Created ticket and draft design. Prioritized as P0 due to upcoming customer audits. Asked infra to estimate snapshot work.

2026-02-17 Elena Gomez (Infra): Snapshot API spike shows two viable approaches: MVCC read view (higher runtime complexity) vs. object-store manifest snapshots (slower but simpler). Prefer manifest approach for initial MVP.
2026-02-24 Arjun Patel (PM): Decided MVP will use object-store manifest snapshots to reduce risk and avoid intrusive datastore changes. Added estimate 8 pts and targeted cycle 2026-W09.

2026-02-28 Daniel Park (Design): Uploaded Console mocks showing 'Simulate purge' modal, progress stream, and downloadable evidence zip. UX includes explicit legal-hold summary and suppression reasons.

2026-03-03 Marcus Lee (Security): Signed off on threat model for simulation runner (read-only enforcement, ephemeral compute, hashed manifests). Security asks for KMS-backed signing and retention of receipts for 7 years by default.
2026-03-05 Arjun Patel: Implementation kickoff. ENG teams assigned. Working PR placeholders created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/purge-sim/pulls
